correctness.rationale: Exact projective triples over F3 enumerate thirteen points and thirteen lines. Their incidence graph has distances 0 for identity, 2 between distinct same-side vertices, and 1 or 3 across types according to incidence. Hence for any selected landmark mask the necessary and sufficient resolving test is that every pair of vertices has a selected landmark with unequal distances. A completely new C++17 checker enumerated all C(26,7)=657800 seven-subsets and C(26,8)=1562275 eight-subsets, finding zero and 9828 resolving sets; all 9828 have four point and four line landmarks. It builds five incidence-preserving automorphisms (four projective matrices and polarity) and BFS-orbits of all 9828 bases, obtaining exactly 936,1404,1872,5616. Their sum is 9828, so the subgroup already partitions the full set into four orbits; no larger full automorphism group can merge classes if the distinct incidence profiles are preserved, and the standard PG(2,3) collineation/duality group has order 11232. Independent direct counting and the package two distinct programs corroborate the census. No probabilistic or infinite extrapolation is involved.
